growth_story.headline: After shrinking from 1990 to 2003, Kenya's income per person has grown since 2004 through repeated shocks, as debt strain and informal work weigh on gains.
growth_story.arc: Kenya's record since 1990 falls into two eras. From 1990 to 2003 income per person fell by 0.9 percent a year, and the World Bank describes a long stagnation that never became a collapse, with donors agreeing that weak economic governance was the main obstacle to development. From 2004 to 2025 it grew by 2.3 percent a year, after what the World Bank calls a move onto a path of accelerating growth after 2002, led by modern services such as mobile telecoms and banking. Shocks broke the run, starting with the violence after the 2007 election, and income per person did not climb back above its 1990 level until 2010. Growth has edged up, from 2.0 percent a year in 2006–2015 to 2.5 in 2016–2025, and income per person reached a new high in 2025. The sources say this steadier growth now sits alongside heavy public debt, a mostly informal job market and, in 2026, new pressure from conflict in the Middle East.

threads.title: Long stagnation, weak governance
threads.text: Income per person drifted down from 1990 to 2003, and by 2003 it was lower than in 1990. The World Bank describes a stagnation that never turned into a crash, and its evaluators recorded donor agreement that poor economic governance was the main obstacle to Kenya's development.

threads.title: The turn after 2002
threads.text: Growth picked up after 2002, and income per person rose every year from 2004 to 2007. The World Bank finds a clear jump in new firms in the 2000s, which it ties to the changed economic climate after the end of the Moi era, and points to new services in mobile telecoms and banking.

threads.title: Shocks that break the run
threads.text: The violence after the 2007 election brought growth to a halt, and income per person growth fell to -2.8 percent in 2008. The pandemic brought -2.2 percent in 2020 before a 5.6 percent rebound in 2021, and the IMF also points to severe droughts and higher import prices.

citations.title: Kenya Country Economic Memorandum: From Economic Growth to Jobs and Shared Prosperity

citations.title: Kenya: Seventh and Eighth Reviews Under the Extended Fund Facility and Extended Credit Facility Arrangements (IMF Country Report No. 24/316)

threads.title: Debt and a squeezed budget
threads.text: In 2024 a tax shortfall, and protests that forced the government to withdraw a finance bill, set back efforts to narrow the budget gap. Interest payments take a large share of revenue, and the World Bank still rates Kenya at high risk of debt distress.

since_last_year.text: Income per person grew 2.6 percent in 2025, though the World Bank says a severe drought late in the year held back farming. Since early 2026, conflict in the Middle East has weighed on the economy, and the World Bank has lowered its growth forecast for 2026. IMF staff visited Nairobi in early 2026 to advance talks on the program Kenya has requested.

growth_story.tension: The sources report total output growing much faster than the 2.6 percent rise in income per person the data show for 2025. The gap is population growth, so the gains spread thinner than the headline growth figures suggest. The sources also describe years of fiscal strain, tax protests and new shocks. Yet the data show income per person growing every year since 2021 and reaching a new high in 2025.
